title: Structure-based virtual screening and drug repurposing studies indicate potential inhibitors of bovine papillomavirus E6 oncoprotein.
authors: de Oliveira Santos, Lucas Alexandre Barbosa; Batista, Marcus Vinicius de Aragao
one_liner_zh: 该研究针对牛乳头瘤病毒E6癌蛋白进行虚拟筛选和药物重定位，虽用分子动力学方法，但对象为蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Bovine papillomavirus type 1 (BPV1) is an oncogenic virus that causes lesions and cancer in infected cattle. Despite being one of the most studied genotypes in the family and occurring in herds worldwide, there are currently no vaccines or drugs for its control. The viral E6 oncoprotein plays a crucial role in infection by this virus, making it a promising target for the development of new therapies. In this regard, we integrated structure-based virtual screening approaches, drug repositioning, and molecular dynamics to identify approved drugs with the potential to inhibit BPV1 E6. Our results reveal that Lumacaftor and MK-3207 are promising candidates for controlling BPV1 infection. The findings of this study may contribute to the development of E6 oncoprotein blockers in an accelerated and cost-effective manner.
abstract_zh: 牛乳头瘤病毒1型（BPV1）是一种致癌病毒，可在受感染的牛中引起病变和癌症。尽管它是该家族中研究最深入的基因型之一，并在全球牛群中普遍存在，但目前尚无疫苗或药物用于其控制。病毒E6癌蛋白在该病毒感染中发挥关键作用，使其成为开发新疗法的有前景靶点。为此，我们整合了基于结构的虚拟筛选方法、药物重定位和分子动力学，以识别具有抑制BPV1 E6潜力的已批准药物。我们的结果表明，Lumacaftor和MK-3207是控制BPV1感染的有前景候选药物。本研究的发现可能有助于以加速且成本有效的方式开发E6癌蛋白阻断剂。
